scope: 1880s default revised after V3-G01 and V3-W01 user feedback: paint marks should construct forms rather than decorate smooth digital illustrations. No controlled image A/B or proven improvement. Historical 2026-11-18 contract preserved unchanged.
prompt: Create ONE original oil painting in a Monet-inspired 1880s painting language. Construct forms through adjoining, overlapping strokes and related colour masses: marks themselves establish planes, weight, light and many edges, instead of decorating a smooth, finished digital illustration with an oil-paint texture. At normal viewing distance keep all requested objects, counts, gestures, main silhouettes, overlaps and proportions readable. Up close let secondary contours emerge from uneven adjacent colour touches, be lost among neighbouring strokes or reappear through contrast. Use broad light-and-shadow relationships as the structure of the paint, not a polished drawing hidden beneath uniform marks. Let quiet, broadly fused or thinner-painted passages coexist with concentrated, directional broken strokes. Do not distribute equal-sized marks across sky, leaves, grass and water simply to make everything look painted. Vary marks where form, material, illumination, distance or visual importance calls for it, not randomly; allow coherent repeated rhythms without a tiled decorative pattern. Form local colour through neighbouring warm/cool, value and reflected-light relations rather than a whole-image pastel tint. Create air and depth from colour, overlap, relative contrast and selective edges, not compulsory haze or digital blur. Keep small figures anatomically and gesturally convincing without miniature photographic faces and outlined fingers. Preserve the specified subject, time, weather, palette and spatial relations. Brushwork need not imply heavy relief: allow modest or thin passages as well as selective surface accents; avoid all-over impasto, fake canvas noise, artificial aging, repeated fish-scales, feathered leaf stamps and neatly combed grass. From a distance the painting should cohere; near the surface its colour strokes should feel integral to the image, not applied afterward.

review_checks.question: Is this a single requested painting with no report layout, charts, tables, labels, split panels or multiple independent compositions?
Does the image satisfy the complete original brief, including objects, count, actions and spatial relations?
Are required structural relationships and, when supplied, the content image identity/composition retained?
Are the requested time, weather and specified colours retained rather than replaced by the reference lighting?
Are forms built through coherent colour/light relationships rather than a uniform tinted filter?
Do marks respond to form, light, distance and visual role, including changes within one material, without arbitrary variation or a repeated stamp across unrelated regions?

Do linked paint strokes and colour masses form the visible shapes, changes of plane, light and edges, or is it a polished smooth illustration with a uniform brush-texture overlay? Judge concrete regions, not colour beauty alone.
Are essential silhouettes, actions and spatial relationships readable while secondary edges can break or merge in a way consistent with the light?
Do colour relationships, overlap, scale and selective edge contrast create scene-appropriate air and depth without forced haze, washed-out distance or uniform blur?
Are foreground/background scale, contrast and atmosphere coherent with the requested scene?
Does detail follow size, distance and visual importance, keeping required identities/actions intact without uniformly polished faces, hands, flowers or clouds, or blanket simplification?

Are brushmark visibility and apparent surface relief handled separately, without uniform thick paint, canvas noise or fabricated aging? Judge appearance only, not actual pigment chemistry or layer history.

After inspecting corners and layout, is the painting free of an unrequested imitation signature or distinctive source composition? Shared requested objects alone are not leakage; mark unclear cases unknown.
Is the image visually decodable and free of unintended text, malformed key objects, framing and other disruptive artifacts?
Is the image free of repeated fish-scale / false micro-texture, gummy patterning, dirty gradients and over-sharpened halos?
